## Our conduct standard

Pinnacle Blooms Network is operated by Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited (BHCL). In these policies, “we”, “us” and “our” mean BHCL in its operation of Pinnacle Blooms Network.

Our people must keep the child’s growing independence and participation at the centre of their work. These public conduct standards explain our expectations; employment-specific terms and procedures belong in the applicable employment documents. This page does not establish an automated tribunal, disciplinary score or certification of every practice.

## Dignity, safety and professional scope

- Respect the child’s comfort, preference and communication, and the family’s dignity. Do not use shame, threats, coercive promises or fabricated outcome claims.

- Work within the relevant role, competence and authorised service. Do not misrepresent qualifications or use a software licence as a professional credential.

- Explain relevant choices, obtain appropriate permissions and report safety or safeguarding concerns through the responsible channels.

## Records, confidentiality and accountability

- Keep assessments, attendance, observations and billing records truthful. Do not backdate, fabricate a result or conceal a material error.

- Access or share personal information only for an authorised purpose. Use approved channels; do not put child records into public chat, personal marketing or social media.

- Disclose relevant conflicts and do not seek improper gifts, commissions or review incentives.

- Take family concerns seriously, cooperate with reviews and do not retaliate for a good-faith concern.

## Raise a conduct concern

Email [care@pinnacleblooms.org](mailto:care@pinnacleblooms.org) with the subject “Staff conduct or care concern”, a way to contact you and the information needed to understand your request. You can call [9100 181 181](tel:+919100181181) for guidance. Do not send passwords, OTPs, full card details or unnecessary child records.

Give the relevant location, role or service and a brief account. A concern is reviewed by responsible management; a privacy matter can be directed to Mr. Gokul Krishna Rao as Privacy Grievance Officer. The applicable process must protect confidentiality and fairness.

## Related policies and updates

[Ethics Charter](/ethics-charter) · [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy) · [Reviews and publication consent](/endorsement-and-testimonial)

This edition is effective from 1 October 2026. It replaces the previous public website wording for this subject. Material changes will be dated here. It does not retrospectively introduce charges or remove rights under an existing agreement.

Nothing in this policy removes a right, remedy, complaint route or protection that applicable law gives you. Booking-specific written terms must be disclosed before you agree; they cannot override mandatory law.

historicalSource.text: 📖 Preface Pinnacle Blooms Network is not a conventional institution. It is the world’s most purpose-driven child development ecosystem — built on 344 skills, 79 abilities, 21 million+ therapy sessions, and a scientifically validated, AI-empowered pathway toward self-sufficiency, school readiness, and mainstream inclusion for children with neurodevelopmental challenges. Behind every AbilityScore® recorded. Behind every session delivered. Behind every parent interaction… …stands a staff member trusted to carry the future of a child. ⚖️ WHY THIS CHARTER EXISTS This Staff Conduct & HR Compliance Charter is the legal, procedural, operational, and ethical foundation that governs how every individual within Pinnacle must act, respond, record, behave, and lead — from entry-level therapist to national leadership. It aligns with: 🏛 Indian Law & IPC Sections (406, 409, 354, etc.) 🌍 WHO and UNICEF codes on Child Safeguarding 🔬 Pinnacle’s proprietary innovations: AbilityScore®, TherapeuticAI®, TherapySphere®, … 📊 IPO-grade audit readiness for Bharath Healthcare P LIMITED 💙 Mother-built, child-first care architecture 🎯 WHAT THIS CHARTER ACHIEVES Codifies non-negotiable behaviors for every role Establishes escalation-ready processes for time, attendance, session integrity, ethics, dress, and data handling Creates a 5-Level Disciplinary Matrix for all violations (L1–L5) Launches a dedicated Conflict of Interest Governance System Ensures legal defensibility of all internal actions (memos, terminations, recoveries, etc.) Protects the Pinnacle promise to parents, partners, policymakers, and children 🧭 WHO THIS CHARTER APPLIES TO Role Covered? All (Speech/OT/ABA/SE/..) Therapists ✅ Yes Admin & Front Office Executives ✅ Yes CT/ DCT/ Center Managers / Zonal Leads ✅ Yes HR, Finance, Ops Teams ✅ Yes National Care Support & BDC Call Teams ✅ Yes SEVA, Outreach, Vendor-facing Staff ✅ Yes For all: If you are part of Pinnacle — this applies to you. 📌 OUR LEGAL POSITION This document shall be considered an official annexure to: Offer Letters Employment Agreements Center Operating Guidelines Ethics Compliance Audits Arbitration or Dispute Proceedings (internal or external) Any breach of this charter is actionable under internal governance systems and applicable Indian law. 🔐 OUR ETHICAL STAND You do not work for Pinnacle. You stand with every mother who cried 912 days to hear “Amma”. You serve not a brand — but a generation waiting to be heard. 📣 DECLARATION At Pinnacle, conduct is not just about compliance. It is about care, consistency, consequence, and courage. This Charter will: Guide the right behavior Correct the wrong behavior Prevent risky behavior Enforce consequences where necessary Protect the dignity of children, families, staff, and the institution 📘 Section 1: Staff Code Of Conduct Universal Charter for Every Staff Member Across Pinnacle Blooms Network 🔍 Purpose To define, mandate, and enforce a unified standard of professional behavior, personal accountability, interpersonal respect, therapeutic precision, and administrative compliance across all employees of Pinnacle Blooms Network. This Code applies across all roles — therapists, center staff, zonal heads, HR, call centers, support teams, vendors, and senior management. ⚖️ Legal Enforceability Treated as a legally binding addendum to every employee’s appointment contract Grounds for disciplinary memo, escalation, suspension, termination, or prosecution based on violation level A primary reference during audits, tribunals, or legal proceedings (internal or external) 📌 Core Behavioral Standards 1.1 Punctuality & Presence All staff must report to duty on time as per center schedules, shift assignments, or therapy calendars. Any delay exceeding 5 minutes must be pre-approved or justified immediately. Every unexcused delay = Level 2 disciplinary memo. 1.2 Biometric & Session Integrity Staff shall log in and out through the official biometric system — without exception. No backdated, pre-punched, or tampered-with entries allowed. Sessions must only be conducted with an assigned child + recorded in platform. Any session conducted without biometric or digital record = ghost session = ethical misconduct. 1.3 Therapy Accuracy & Documentation Every single therapy session must be conducted as per the TherapeuticAI session Plan Only. Session entries must reflect real therapy delivered. No copy-paste, delay, manipulation, or proxy entries allowed. AbilityScore® Refresh must be completed within 24 hours since pending. TherapeuticAI® Homework input must be completed within 5 minutes of the session. Inaccurate, pending, neglected, stalled, or delayed documentation = clinical negligence. 1.4 Dress & Appearance Uniform (if applicable) or formal professional dress code is mandatory. No chappals/slippers, faded t-shirts, flashy accessories, or improper grooming on the therapy floor. Every single violation = memo. 1.5 Language & Respect Language must always be respectful, non-judgmental, free of sarcasm, ridicule, threat, or frustration. Always address parents as “Sir / Madam” or regional equivalents like “Amma / Nanna” with dignity. 1.6 Confidentiality No staff shall discuss, display, forward, or share child data, session videos, parent phone numbers, or therapy reports on personal WhatsApp, email, social media, or any other unauthorized channel by all means. Violation = direct escalation to HR + Ethics Committee + IPC prosecution. 1.7 Mobile Phone & Device Policy No mobile usage allowed during therapy. Devices must remain on silent or airplane mode. Taking calls in session is grounds for memo unless it is emergency-approved. 1.8 Interpersonal Conduct Gossip, personal fights, toxic behavior, center-level favoritism, political conversations, religious bias, or caste-based talk is strictly prohibited. Interpersonal conflicts must be escalated to center head or HR — not left to fester on-floor. 1.9 Parent Handling Protocol Never promise, diagnose, or speculate. Never say: “Your child is autistic” “She won’t speak” “We’ll cure him in 2 months” All feedback must be routed through AbilityScore Report, AbilityScore 7 Readiness Indexes Report, CT/DCT/center in-charge or designated therapist. 1.10 Financial Decorum No staff shall accept any gift, cash, donation, or informal payment from any parent or vendor — regardless of amount. Accepting a gift above ₹50 = Conflict of Interest = mandatory report. 🚨 Mandatory Conduct Declaration Every staff member shall sign the following statement upon onboarding, and during annual compliance training: “I acknowledge that I have read, understood, and accepted the Staff Code of Conduct. I understand that failure to comply may result in disciplinary action including warning, suspension, termination, or legal prosecution depending on the severity of violation.” 📊 Link to Disciplinary Matrix Each clause above shall map directly to the 5-Level Disciplinary Action System in Section 7. For example: Violation of 1.2 (Biometric Tampering) = Level 4 Violation of 1.6 (Data Breach) = Level 5 Violation of 1.9 (Improper parent assurance) = Level 3 or 4 based on impact All violations shall be processed via official memo, recorded in HRMS, and linked to the employee’s performance appraisal, promotion eligibility, and retention review. 🕰 Section 2: Time & Attendance Policy Precision in Presence. Trust in Timelines. Excellence in Execution. 📖 Purpose At Pinnacle Blooms Network, every minute counts — because every missed minute delays a child’s milestone. This policy exists to: Enforce a scientific, shift-based, biometrically accountable system of staff presence Ensure therapy continuity, center discipline, and parental trust Maintain legal and procedural records for HR, audit, and escalation purposes 🔐 Coverage Therapists (Speech, OT, ABA, Behavioral, Special Educators) Admin Executives & Receptionists Center Heads & Zonal Leads Customer Care Executives Operations, HR, Finance Staff National or remote team members on virtual/rotational schedules 🧾 Definitions Term Definition Shift Assigned duty hours per role: Full-time / Half-day / Rotational Biometric Log Official in/out entry through Pinnacle-approved biometric device or mobile OTP Session Lag Time between scheduled therapy and actual login/delivery Unplanned Leave Leave not pre-approved in Pinnacle Platform Comp Off Time off granted in lieu of approved extra duty hours Attendance Violation Any form of delay, absence, ghost entry, buddy punching, or falsified presence 🧭 Attendance Expectations by Role Role Check-in Time Shift Closure Max Acceptable Delay Therapists 8:45 AM (for 9 AM first session) Post last session + logs 5 min grace (2×/month) Admin/Front Office 8:30 AM Until therapy closes 5 min grace Center Head/ CT/ DCT 8:15 AM Post therapist close 0 min delay tolerance Call Center Based on rotation (start-of-shift login required) Full shift required System-monitored HR/National/Finance 8:30 AM As per roster or assigned model 10 min remote flex window (only WFH model) 🛑 Rules & Enforcement Clauses 2.1 Biometric is Mandatory Every employee must log in and out via biometric (or OTP log if remote) “Forgot to punch” is not valid. Repeat = misconduct. 2.2 No Proxy or Buddy Punching Logging in for another employee or colluding = Level 4 violation (Fraud) 2.3 Late Reporting Every instance of delay (> 5 mins) = L2 memo Three+ delays in a month = eligibility freeze for performance-linked incentives 2.4 Session Delay Therapists who arrive after child scheduled time will be penalized via: Memo + Session Recovery Instruction Alert to Zonal Team on missed therapy Parent apology protocol initiated 2.5 Early Exit without Closure Leaving without log-out, pending sessions, or therapy notes = L2 violation Includes walking out for personal reasons without approval in Pinnacle platform. Three+ early exits in a month = eligibility freeze for performance-linked incentives 2.6 Unapproved Leaves Unapproved leave tagged as Absent Without Authorization (AWA) attracts double deduction 📊 Attendance Review System (ARS) Each center will maintain a monthly dashboard that flags: Top 5 punctual staff Top 5 delayed entries Repeat offenders with escalation tiers Biometric-device gap vs schedule discrepancy This data will be: Shared with NCC, BEDC, Finance, HR, Leadership teams in real-time, refreshed every 2 seconds. Linked to appraisal and increment matrix Used to flag escalation to Ethics or Officer Relevant if falsification is suspected 🧮 Exceptions (Subject to Documentation) Scenario Valid Action Medical Emergency Notify via official SR; submit doctor certificate Family Death Bereavement leave request; death certificate copy if available Public Transport Strike News clip proof + alternate travel attempt documentation All exceptions must be updated in Pinnacle within 24 hours or they become invalid. 📍 Escalation Flow Violation Escalation Authority First-time delay L1 Written Memo 3+ delays L2 Written Memo + Recovery Timeline 5+ delays L3 Memo + Zonal Escalation Ghost session or proxy entry L5 memo + Escalation to Ethics Panel Biometric tampering L5 memo + Prosecution/Legal Referral 🖋 Declaration “I understand that my time and presence are not just procedural — they are fundamental to a child’s developmental progress. I commit to full compliance with Pinnacle’s Time & Attendance Policy. I accept that violations may result in disciplinary or legal action.” 🧬 Section 3: Therapy Session Integrity Policy Protecting the Science. Honoring the Child. Upholding the Brand. 📖 PURPOSE At Pinnacle Blooms Network, therapy sessions are not just clinical appointments. They are scientifically recorded interventions, directly feeding into: The child’s AbilityScore® The personalized therapy path via TherapeuticAI® The long-term developmental plan of over 344 skills and 79 abilities This policy ensures accuracy, accountability, and audit-readiness of every therapy session — to uphold trust with parents, protect scientific integrity, and ensure ethical therapy delivery across 21 million+ sessions. ⚖ LEGAL FRAMEWORK Fully enforceable under Indian Evidence Act (as therapy logs are medical-legal records) Governed by The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 Subject to Data Protection, Employment, and Clinical Ethics Laws Auditable under upcoming IPO-readiness protocols, MoWCD audits, and private investor diligence 🎯 SCOPE Speech, OT, ABA, Sensory Integration, Behavioral, and Special Education Therapists Zonal and Center-Level Therapy Leads Documentation, Reception & Therapy Admin Staff Customer Care and Feedback Analysts TherapeuticAI® Users and Intervention Designers 📌 NON-NEGOTIABLE THERAPY PROTOCOL STANDARDS 3.1 Session Validity Criteria Status Scheduled in official Pinnacle System YES Child leave or grace sessions marked in Pinnacle YES Therapist biometrically logged in YES Session occurred in designated room/space YES Therapy homework log entered on same day YES AbilityScore® updated (if applicable) YES Parent feedback tracked (verbal/logged) YES Any session not meeting these = INVALID SESSION = Audit Red Flag. 3.2 Forbidden Practices (Strictly Prohibited) Code Violation Level 🔴 TSI-01 Ghost session logging (child not present) L5 🔴 TSI-02 Backdated session entry L4 🔴 TSI-03 Inserting fabricated progress L4 🔴 TSI-04 Therapy done but not entered (data loss) L3 🔴 TSI-05 Sharing therapy insights on personal WhatsApp L3 🔴 TSI-06 Writing notes without real therapy observed L5 🔴 TSI-07 Leaking any / all kind of kid, parent, family information L5 Each of these constitutes data tampering, ethical breach, and in some cases, child neglect. 3.3 Scientific Fidelity Requirements Therapy homework must accurately reflect: Techniques therapied; skill categories addressed Child’s response Intervention attempted Homework plan for parents, families Must be entered: Within 5 minutes of session In the assigned Pinnacle TherapeuticAI platform only Session time ≠ scheduled time: 40-minute session must be 40 minutes active time Anything < 50% duration = partial session 🧪 ABILITYSCORE® & THERAPEUTICAI® GUIDED Every session directly affects AbilityScore® trajectory Every session alters TherapeuticAI® recommendations Every session modifies parent trust and expectation Falsifying a session breaks this ecosystem, risks a child’s future plan, and is treated as clinical-level fraud. 📊 THERAPY QUALITY INDEX (TQI) MONITORING Metric Target Frequency Session log completion rate 100% within 5 mins Daily Session audit accuracy 95%+ accurate Monthly Backdate occurrence 0% Real-time Flagged inconsistencies <1% Escalated immediately Zonal therapy auditors will randomly sample 5% of logs weekly for non-following of TherapeuticAI/session program, time mismatch, missing/wrong Fusion Module (Therapist Clinical Expertise 1* to 5* rating of the interventions in each program). 🚨 ESCALATION PROTOCOLS Violation Type First Offense Repeat Missed/pending log L2 Memo L3 Memo + Recovery Coaching Backdated entry L3 Memo L4 + Session audit for 30 days Ghost session L5 Memo + Penalty Prosecution + Legal Action Not following TherapeuticAI L4 Memo Performance Freeze + Ethics Review Inaccurate child feedback Ethics Memo Recorded Case Panel 🧾 SESSION INTEGRITY DECLARATION “I understand that every therapy note I write becomes part of a child’s developmental map. I pledge that I will only log sessions that I have personally delivered, with full honesty, attention, and respect for the trust reposed in me by families and Pinnacle.” 🔐 AUDIT LINKAGE All session logs are linked to AbilityScore® changes All session logs are mapped to session videos (if enabled) All session logs are monitored for log-ins/out, time match, and parent feedback mismatch 📣 CLOSING STATEMENT Every session entered without integrity is not a data error — it’s a betrayal of the child. It breaks a sacred contract between science, service, and soul. Pinnacle will treat it with the seriousness it deserves. 👔 Section 4: Appearance & Behavior Policy Professional Dignity. Therapeutic Decorum. Culture of Confidence. 📖 Purpose In a system like Pinnacle — built on trust, transparency, and therapeutic science — appearance and behavior are not cosmetic. They are clinical cues. They directly influence: Parent, Family confidence Child comfort Center discipline Pinnacle brand reputation This policy ensures that every staff member — therapist or admin, junior or senior — embodies professional presence and behavioral clarity reflective of Pinnacle’s position as India’s most trusted and scientifically proven child development network. ⚖ Legal & Organizational Framework Labor contract codes Internal disciplinary governance protocols Rights of Children to Safe Environments Act (2021 Draft Provisions) Indian employment ethics and Center SOPs Brand usage and public-facing standards of Bharath Healthcare P LIMITED 👥 Applicability All center-based and teleconsultation staff Admins, therapists, call center agents Supervisors, zonal heads, and national teams when visiting centers or parents Public representatives of Pinnacle at schools, exhibitions, and campaigns 👗 Dress Code Policy 4.1 Therapist & Floor Staff Item Requirement Top Solid-color kurta / lab coat / Pinnacle uniform Bottom Plain trousers or leggings (no jeans, no see-through fabrics) Footwear Clean formal closed-toe shoes. No slippers or flip-flops. Hair Tied back neatly (especially for child-facing roles) Accessories Minimal. No dangling earrings, strong perfumes, or flashy items. ID Badge must be visibly worn during all working hours 4.2 Admin & Front Desk Must wear formal Indian or Western attire; no slogans, political, or religious symbols Formal or business-casual footwear Hair & hygiene neat, presentable, and consistent with front-desk expectations 4.3 Call Center / Remote Staff Dress formally during Zoom/video calls with parents or school coordinators Background must be neutral, well-lit, and devoid of distractions or personal clutter 🔇 Verbal Etiquette Standards 4.4 Universal Speech Conduct Speak clearly, gently, and professionally No slang, regional taunts, or mimicking of child/parent behavior No excessive familiarity or inappropriate jokes in parent presence Use professional terms only (e.g., “session”, “therapy”, “support plan”) 4.5 Mandatory Phrases Address parents as “Sir”, “Madam”, “Amma”, or “Nanna” per preference Always thank the parent after each session “Do you have any feedback or need anything from us?” — must be asked every Wednesday 🧭 Behavioral Standards Within Centers Behavior Status Sitting idly during working hours ❌ Prohibited Engaging in personal phone/video calls on the floor ❌ Prohibited Talking loudly or laughing disruptively near therapy rooms ❌ Prohibited Complaining about other staff in front of parents ❌ Prohibited Complimenting, comforting, or guiding a parent respectfully ✅ Encouraged 🚷 Prohibited Behavior Code Violation Action Level AB-01 Sarcastic remarks to parents L4 Memo AB-02 Dress-code violation (>2) L2 Memo + Re-induction AB-03 Center gossip, groupism, or bias L4 Memo + HR Coaching AB-04 Touching child without therapeutic context or consent L5 Ethics Escalation AB-05 Body shaming, colorism, or caste-based talk L4/L5 Suspension AB-06 Posting center/child photos without authorization L5 + Legal AB-07 Use of offensive tone with HR/parents/staff L3→L4 Escalation 📊 Center Discipline Audit (CDA) Each center’s Zonal Admin or Discipline Officer shall submit a monthly audit: Dress code compliance (random weekly check) Video call posture (call center or remote staff) Behavior-based parent feedback snippets Hygiene and grooming infra report (including fragrance-free zones) This will be included in center grading and staff performance reviews. 📩 Parent-Facing Situations Policy In any interaction — whether in person, on phone, or on video — staff must: Sit or stand with respectful posture Avoid interrupting the parent Smile gently, not forcefully Never offer a medical label or false hope End every interaction with a warm “Thank you for trusting us” 📜 Declaration to be Signed Onboarding & Annually “I understand that my appearance, tone, and demeanor shape the way a child and parent experiences Pinnacle. I commit to conduct myself with full dignity, compassion, and professionalism every time I wear the Pinnacle ID.” 💬 Closing Statement A child sees more than we say. A parent observes more than we intend. And in every moment — you are not just a staff member. You are the face of India’s most trusted child empowerment network. Dress like it. Speak like it. Be it. 📱 Section 5: Device, Internet & Communication Policy Protecting Privacy. Enabling Precision. Enforcing Platform Discipline. 📖 Purpose In a digital-first therapeutic environment like Pinnacle Blooms Network — where AbilityScore®, TherapeuticAI®, and session logs are driven by real-time data — personal devices, internet use, and communication must be governed with absolute integrity. ✅ Secure handling of sensitive child data ✅ Controlled use of digital communication tools ✅ Prevention of distraction during therapy ✅ Elimination of unauthorized media or content sharing ✅ Enforcement of IT and information security governance across all roles ⚖️ Legal & Organizational Coverage Indian Information Technology Act, 2000 Indian Clinical Privacy & Data Protection Guidelines (MoHFW Draft) Internal Cyber & Communication Control Charter Evidence Act (as therapy logs and recordings are legally admissible) 👥 Who This Policy Applies To Category Applicability Therapists, HR, Finance ✅ Yes Admin & Reception ✅ Yes Call Center Executives ✅ Yes Center Heads & Zonal Leads ✅ Yes National Staff, NCC, BDC ✅ Yes Vendors & External Trainers ✅ Yes (as observers or guests) 📲 Device Usage Policy 5.1 Mobile Phones Rule Enforcement No phones during active therapy sessions Mandatory — silenced, airplane mode or off Phone use only during lunch breaks Permitted if not delaying any session No recording, photos, screenshots inside therapy rooms or of Pinnacle Prohibited unless authorized Phones kept out of reach of children Mandatory Call Center Agents wear headsets, mute ambient noise Required 5.2 Personal Laptops / Tablets Not permitted on therapy floors No offline bookkeeping, note-taking, or record keeping Personal devices cannot store therapy-related content 🌐 Internet & Platform Access 5.3 Approved Platforms Purpose Platform Session Logging & AbilityScore® Pinnacle Official Portal / App Official Communication Service Request, Memo, care@pinnacleblooms.org, 9100181181 Internal Updates Telegram Groups (Staff, Admin, Relevant Group), Personal Handle Training Pinnacle Platform, Miracles, Certified Training Courses, Internal Academy Tool 5.4 Prohibited Sites No external streaming platforms (Netflix, YouTube, Instagram) during shift No cryptocurrency, betting, or unethical sites from center IPs No downloading or storing pirated content, therapy tools, or games 💬 Communication Etiquette Policy 5.5 Internal Chat Groups (WhatsApp / Slack / Telegram) Rule Enforcement Group name must be official (e.g., “Pinnacle – Center – Admin”) Mandatory No memes, good morning spam, or religious content Strictly Prohibited No private therapy discussions or parent gossip Strictly Prohibited Zonal Admin/HR must be group moderators Required Staff must exit group after resignation Mandatory (within 24 hrs) 5.6 Parent Communications All official updates through Pinnacle official handle WhatsApp only for session reminders, feedback, approved therapy coordination Never share PDFs, dashboard screenshots, photos/videos without SR authorization All messages must be professional, signed with name and designation Example: “Thank you. Regards, Sangeetha – Occupational Therapist, Pinnacle Suchitra Center” 🔐 Information Security 5.7 Sensitive Data Protocols Child session videos, audio clips, screen shares are confidential assets Access to internal therapy reports restricted to assigned roles Device loss/theft reported within 1 hour to zonal IT & HR via SR No printing or downloading child records on personal drives 5.8 External Communication Control Media interviews, school visits, blog posts, public webinars pre-approved by National Care Center Speaking on behalf of Pinnacle without authorization = Level 4 violation 🧾 Device & Chat Violations Matrix Code Violation Level DIC-01 Using phone during therapy L2 DIC-02 Sharing child video/photo on WhatsApp L5 DIC-03 Unauthorized Zoom session with parent L4 DIC-04 Gossiping in team group about parent/staff L3 DIC-05 Personal files on therapy computer L3 📊 Tech & Communication Compliance Audits Monthly digital audits will verify: Unauthorized devices on floor (surprise inspection) Session log timestamp mismatches WhatsApp screenshot logs (HR-monitored groups) CRM usage vs phone follow-up gaps Response etiquette in call logs and email threads 🖋 Declaration of Compliance “I understand that phones, devices, data, and messages are not casual tools — they are windows into a child’s therapy experience and Pinnacle’s credibility. I commit to full compliance with the Device, Internet & Communication Policy.” 📣 Closing Statement Every message you send. Every session you log. Every phone call you make becomes part of a child’s record — and part of Pinnacle’s reputation. Act accordingly. Log responsibly. Communicate with care. 🔐 Section 6: Confidentiality & Data Handling Policy Privacy Is a Right. Data Is a Responsibility. Protection Is the Pinnacle Standard. 📖 PURPOSE Pinnacle Blooms Network handles the most sacred form of data — a child’s developmental reality. From session videos to parent discussions, from AbilityScore® records to therapy logs — every byte represents a family’s vulnerability, trust, and hope. This policy governs the collection, usage, access, storage, transmission, and destruction of sensitive personal and therapy-related data across Pinnacle’s nationwide and global operations — and ensures full compliance with law, ethics, and scientific accountability. ⚖️ LEGAL & REGULATORY BASIS Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures) Rules, 2011 – India Personal Data Protection Bill – Draft (India, 2023) The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 MoWCD Child Privacy Guidelines Pinnacle’s Global IP, Scientific & Clinical Governance Framework 🧠 SCOPE OF PROTECTION Data Type Examples 🎯 Personally Identifiable Info (PII) Child name, age, school, diagnosis, family member details 🎥 Visual & Audio Content Recorded therapy clips, parent sessions, audio feedback 📊 Scientific & Clinical Records AbilityScore®, session logs, Behavioral Observations 📄 Financial & Consent Data Invoice data, SEVA documentation, parental approvals 🗣️ Conversations Parent reports, therapist opinions, center discussions 📌 CORE POLICIES 6.1 Access Control Rule Enforcement Only authorized therapists may view/edit a child’s session logs Mandatory TherapeuticAI®, AbilityScore® can only be accessed by the assigned team Enforced via login control Center Heads cannot view children from other centers Geo-role locked Data must be accessed only from official systems Personal laptop/tablet usage = Prohibited 6.2 Storage & Transfer Therapy logs must be entered only into Pinnacle’s secure platform No offline records unless expressly authorized Any physical records must be stored in locked, access-controlled cabinets Data must never be transferred over: WhatsApp; Gmail/Outlook personal ID; Google Drive personal; USB drives, external HDDs, or pen drives 6.3 Destruction Policy Expired session notes (beyond retention period) must be shredded/digitally purged Unused physical reports must be destroyed by center head in HR-verified protocol Exit staff must surrender all physical/digital data upon last working day 6.4 Parent Consent Management Every child must have a signed or digitally acknowledged consent form prior to any: Assessment; AbilityScore® screening; Therapy initiation; Video recording Consent forms are stored in the parent CRM and governed by data retention SOP 🚫 STRICTLY PROHIBITED ACTIONS Code Violation Level CDH-01 Taking session video on personal phone L5 CDH-02 Sharing child’s report with non-family via WhatsApp L5 CDH-03 Discussing a child’s diagnosis in front of other parents L5 CDH-04 Leaving paper files open on front desk L5 CDH-05 Forwarding any child image to other therapists L5 CDH-06 Carrying session logs home without approval L5 📊 DATA ACCESS MONITORING & AUDITS Activity Frequency Audit Team System login & download trace Weekly IT + Compliance Random session note access review Monthly Zonal Audit Child file visual security check Surprise audits HR + Center Head Exit compliance (Data surrender audit) Per exit Admin + Zonal Audit reports are reviewed quarterly by the Ethics & Information Security Committee. 🧾 THIRD-PARTY & VENDOR CLAUSE Any third-party trainer, app, or tech provider accessing child data must sign Pinnacle’s Data Handling NDA, submit monthly audit of access log, and be approved by National Compliance Office Failure = Contract Termination + Legal Notice 📋 STAFF DECLARATION (TO BE SIGNED DIGITALLY & ONBOARDING) “I understand that child data is not mine. It is protected, personal, and governed by law and ethics. I shall access it only when required for therapeutic duty and never share, misuse, or expose it without express written consent from authorized personnel.” 📣 CLOSING STATEMENT The world runs on information. But at Pinnacle, we run on confidentiality. Because what you carelessly forward today… might be a child’s future case file, a parent’s privacy risk, or a national-level ethics breach tomorrow.
